evidence.detail: rs/C enqueues into rs/m/a from its live AWT mouse/key input handlers, including press/release, motion/drag and key-event paths, passing event type, button/key code, coordinates and event timestamps.

The class owns a fixed 256-entry rs/m/a$a ring, synchronized enqueue/reset/drain operations, and coalesces consecutive type-3 movement records while preserving min/max x/y bounds and latest timestamp.
Client.by() drains rs/m/a into its preallocated record array before the normal input/game-tick path, then applies record types 1..5 to live mouse-button, release, pointer/movement and key state.
The class is not network telemetry or rendering state; it is the synchronized handoff queue between AWT input callbacks and Client input processing.

candidates.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for the synchronized AWT-to-client input event queue.

evidence.detail: Each record stores event type, button/key code, current x/y, movement min/max x/y bounds and timestamp; enqueue initializes these fields and movement coalescing widens the bounds.
InputEventQueue owns exactly 256 preallocated records and copies queued record state into Client's drain buffer.
Client.by() branches on the record type and consumes the stored code, coordinates, bounds and timestamp to update live input state.

candidates.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for one buffered client input event record.
